sections.label: Audit findings
paragraphs: I audited Weld's existing assets and looked at how competitors positioned themselves. Icons, colors, and hierarchy were inconsistent. The site felt like several people had designed it with no shared direction.

sections.label: Competitive analysis
paragraphs: I looked at direct and indirect competitors: what worked, what felt dated, and where Weld could stand apart. Everyone else was trying to look serious. That left room for personality.

sections.label: Website clarity
paragraphs: The priority was clarity: what Weld does, who it's for, and why they should care. Each page had one job, whether that was explaining features, showing pricing, or getting people to sign up.

sections.label: Brand refresh
paragraphs: I refreshed the visual identity with a bold palette and clean typography. The logo stayed. Everything around it got tighter, and custom icons and illustration added character without losing credibility.

sections.label: Design system foundation
paragraphs: The brand system became a Figma library: components, grids, color tokens, and icons. Prototyping got faster, and developers had a clear handoff.

sections.label: Website redesign
paragraphs: Homepage, pricing, signup, resources, and product pages were rebuilt on the new identity. Navigation was clarified, and the information architecture was reworked so visitors could find what they needed.

sections.label: Brand personality
paragraphs: Custom icons and illustrations supported the copy instead of replacing it. Infographics carried the harder ideas. The result stayed professional, but not cold.

sections.label: Foundation for growth
paragraphs: New features and pages could ship from the design system instead of starting over. The brand stayed consistent across the website and the product.

sections.label: Clear communication
paragraphs: The website finally said what Weld did and why anyone should use it. Across the redesign, the message was the same: Weld is the trustworthy way to connect your data tools.
